title: City Council Approves Riverside Solar Farm After Yearlong Debate
text:
The Sunnyvale city council voted 6-3 on Tuesday night to approve a 120-acre solar farm on the former Riverside gravel pit, clearing the largest renewable energy project in county history. The decision capped a yearlong debate that drew packed hearings and dueling petitions. Supporters said the solar farm will power roughly eleven thousand homes and cut the city's carbon emissions by nearly a fifth. Opponents argued the project would erase farmland and drag down nearby property values.

Construction is expected to begin next spring once state regulators sign off on the site plan. The developer, Meridian Renewables, agreed to fund a new access road and to plant native grasses around the panel arrays. Council member Dana Reyes, who cast the deciding vote, said the compromise addressed most neighborhood concerns about drainage and traffic.

Community response was divided but measured. About sixty residents attended the Tuesday session, and several thanked the council for months of open hearings. The county farmers association said it still plans to file an appeal over lost agricultural land. A petition opposing the solar farm gathered two thousand signatures.

City staff expect the solar farm to reach full output by late 2027. The council will revisit its approval in one year to weigh production data and community complaints.
reference: The Sunnyvale city council approved a large solar farm on the old Riverside gravel pit after a yearlong debate.
